source: Bhagavata Purana 8.16.15-23; 8.17.8-18 (Bhaktivedanta Book Trust translation); https://vedabase.io/en/library/sb/8/16/; https://vedabase.io/en/library/sb/8/17/
comments: Aditi asks for protection and restoration for her existing sons. In 8.17.18 Vishnu offers to become her son. The quoted petitions do not explicitly request a new male child; the chapter summary describes the episode more broadly as her request.

source: Luke 1:5-13; https://biblehub.com/kjv/luke/1.htm
comments: Luke 1:13 says the prayer was heard and announces a son, but does not quote a request specifying the child's sex. Unspecified concerns the recorded petition, not the announced child.

source: The Book of Dede Korkut, Legend I (Faruk Sumer, Ahmet E. Uysal and Warren S. Walker translation, University of Texas Press, 1972), opening feast and birth episode; https://mughal-library.s3.me-central-1.amazonaws.com/Images/ebooks/pdfs/ebook_the_book_of_dede_korkut_BxknuEC.pdf#page=32
comments: In this translation both Dirse Khan and his wife explicitly express a wish for a healthy son before the feast and collective prayer. Their son is then born. Replaced the unverified Lewis-edition reference with the translation inspected; the son coding is unchanged.

source: Genesis 16:2-4,10-15 (KJV); https://biblehub.com/kjv/genesis/16.htm
comments: Sarai proposes obtaining children through Hagar; Hagar is already pregnant when the angel announces Ishmael. No explicit request for a son is recorded in this episode. Included as a birth announcement, not evidence of a sex-specific petition.

source: Genesis 17:16-19; 21:1-3 (KJV); https://biblehub.com/kjv/genesis/17.htm; https://biblehub.com/kjv/genesis/21.htm
comments: God promises a son through Sarah. Abraham's spoken request in 17:18 concerns the already-born Ishmael; it is not a request for Isaac to be male.

source: 1 Samuel 1:10-20 (KJV); https://biblehub.com/kjv/1_samuel/1.htm
comments: The vow explicitly asks for a male child in verse 11; verse 20 identifies Samuel as the resulting son. Later children in 1 Samuel 2:21 are outside this episode.

source: Genesis 25:21-26 (KJV); https://biblehub.com/kjv/genesis/25.htm
comments: Isaac prays because Rebekah is childless; the passage does not quote a sex-specific petition. Verses 24-26 identify the twins Esau and Jacob.

source: Judges 13:3-24 (KJV); https://biblehub.com/kjv/judges/13.htm
comments: An angel announces a son before Manoah prays for instructions about raising the child in 13:8. The announcement does not establish a prior request for a son.

source: Genesis 30:1,22-24 (KJV); https://biblehub.com/kjv/genesis/30.htm
comments: Verse 1 asks Jacob for children without specifying sex; verse 22 reports God hearing Rachel, but does not quote her prayer. Joseph is the outcome; the expressed hope for another son in verse 24 is coded in the separate second episode.

source: Genesis 30:24; 35:16-18; https://biblehub.com/kjv/genesis/30.htm; https://biblehub.com/kjv/genesis/35.htm
comments: The request or expressed hope for another son occurs when Joseph is named in Genesis 30:24. Genesis 35 narrates Benjamin's birth, not a prayer in labor. Linking the passages is a narrative coding choice.

source: Mahabharata, Adi Parva, section CLXIX (Kisari Mohan Ganguli translation); https://sacred-texts.com/hin/m01/m01170.htm
comments: Drupada explicitly requests a son able to kill Drona. Dhrishtadyumna and Draupadi emerge from the sacrifice. No daughter is requested in his quoted petition; the queen subsequently asks to be recognized as mother of both children.

source: Mahabharata, Adi Parva, Sambhava Parva, sections CXV-CXVI (Kisari Mohan Ganguli translation); https://sacred-texts.com/hin/m01/m01116.htm; https://sacred-texts.com/hin/m01/m01117.htm
comments: Initially requests 100 sons; subsequently wishes for a daughter while Vyasa divides the mass. Dushala is explicitly desired in section CXVI. This row combines the successive wishes within the same birth episode.

source: Mahabharata, Adi Parva, sections CXXII-CXXIII (Kisari Mohan Ganguli translation); https://sacred-texts.com/hin/m01/m01123.htm; https://sacred-texts.com/hin/m01/m01124.htm
comments: Pandu explicitly anticipates a son when directing the invocation in CXXII, and Kunti assents. Her direct request to Dharma in CXXIII uses offspring. Son coding includes Pandu's stated aim, not Kunti's words alone.

source: Mahabharata, Adi Parva, section CXXIII (Kisari Mohan Ganguli translation); https://sacred-texts.com/hin/m01/m01124.htm
comments: Pandu explicitly desires a superior son and performs austerities; Kunti observes the vow and invokes Indra. Sex-specific intent is stated before the divine promise.

source: Mahabharata, Adi Parva, Sambhava Parva, section CXI (Kisari Mohan Ganguli translation); https://sacred-texts.com/hin/m01/m01112.htm
comments: Kunti says she invoked Surya to test the formula and asks pardon; she then resists his request. Karna is born afterward. This account does not establish an intended pregnancy or a sex-specific request; unspecified should not be read as an affirmative wish for a child.

source: Mahabharata, Adi Parva, section CXXIII (Kisari Mohan Ganguli translation); https://sacred-texts.com/hin/m01/m01124.htm
comments: Pandu requests strong offspring; Kunti asks Vayu for a strong, large-limbed child in this translation. The martial context permits a male-child interpretation, but unspecified follows the explicit request wording rather than inferring sex from strength or Bhima's birth.

source: Mahabharata, Adi Parva, section CXXIV (Kisari Mohan Ganguli translation); https://sacred-texts.com/hin/m01/m01125.htm
comments: Madri asks for offspring and invokes the twin gods after Kunti shares the formula. Two sons result. Unspecified follows the quoted request wording; the lineage and funeral-rite context may support a male-heir interpretation.

ritual_type: request to revive an already-born child
source: Mahabharata, Ashvamedhika Parva, sections LXVIII-LXIX (Kisari Mohan Ganguli translation); https://sacred-texts.com/hin/m14/m14068.htm; https://sacred-texts.com/hin/m14/m14069.htm
comments: Uttara asks Krishna to revive the child already born dead and addresses him as her son. Son coding concerns this particular existing child, not a preference for the sex of a future birth. The count is one revived child, not an additional conception or birth.

source: Quran, As-Saffat 37:100-101 (Mustafa Khattab, The Clear Quran); https://quran.com/en/as-saffat/100-101
comments: The cited translation renders the petition as a request for righteous offspring; the response announces a son. Coding follows explicit request wording in this translation. Some translations supply son in the petition. The son is not named in these verses.

source: Quran, Hud 11:71 (Mustafa Khattab, The Clear Quran); https://quran.com/en/hud/71
comments: Announcement of Isaac to Ibrahim's wife, without a quoted request specifying sex. Jacob is a later descendant, not an additional son of this couple.

source: Quran, Maryam 19:5-7; Al Imran 3:38-39 (Mustafa Khattab, The Clear Quran); https://quran.com/maryam/5; https://quran.com/en/ali-imran/38
comments: The cited translation requests an heir in 19:5 and good offspring in 3:38; the subsequent announcement specifies John. Unspecified means no explicit request for a son or daughter under this wording rule; it does not rule out a male-heir interpretation of the passage.

source: Valmiki Ramayana, Bala Kanda 1.15.1-3; 1.16.27-31; 1.18.8-16 (valmikiramayan.net Sanskrit and English translation); https://www.valmikiramayan.net/utf8/baala/sarga15/balasans15.htm; https://www.valmikiramayan.net/utf8/baala/sarga16/balasans16.htm; https://www.valmikiramayan.net/utf8/baala/sarga18/balasans18.htm
comments: The rite explicitly aims at sons. Dasharatha distributes the sacrificial food among Kausalya, Kaikeyi and Sumitra; the birth passage assigns Rama, Bharata, and the twins Lakshmana and Shatrughna respectively. Counts the four births from this episode, not all children in other accounts.

ritual_type: tapas to obtain Shiva as husband
source: Shiva Purana 2.3.22.13-17, 57-59; 2.4.2.55-70 (J. L. Shastri translation); https://www.wisdomlib.org/hinduism/book/shiva-purana-english/d/doc226086.html; https://www.wisdomlib.org/hinduism/book/shiva-purana-english/d/doc226122.html
comments: Corrected son request to unspecified: the stated aim of this penance is to obtain Shiva, not a sex-specific request for a child. Kartikeya/Guha belongs to the later birth narrative, where Shiva's seed passes through Agni, six sages' wives, Himavat and Ganga before a boy appears among reeds. Retained as a related penance and birth narrative, not evidence that Parvati prayed for a son or gave birth to Kartikeya herself. The outcome fields describe the associated child; they do not establish that this was an answered fertility petition.
